Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as if conjunction

also as though, like (as if), as it were, under the pretext that, on the pretext that

classical

Ter. Eun. 3.2.8: assimulābō, quasi nunc exeam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 5.43: in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus
Traupman 106: he left under the pretext that …, hinc abiit quasi (+ subj.)

quasi

conjunction, with the subjunctive in the tense the main verb calls for; without a verb, “as it were”

as if; as it were

“As if” with a clause: the verb is subjunctive, present or perfect after a present main verb (not the imperfect of English “as if he were”). Without a verb it softens a word used loosely: quasi scintillās, “sparks, as it were”.

Other words

  • tamquam (tamquam sī) — as if; like

    conjunction, with the subjunctive; without a verb, “like” · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42: parvī enim prīmō ortū sīc jacent, tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint; Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

  • velut (velut sī) — as if; like

    conjunction, with the subjunctive; without a verb, “like” · also used · classical · Liv. 1.56.12: velut sī prōlāpsus cecidisset, terram ōsculō contigit; Liv. 5.41.9: ad eōs velut simulācra versī

    Livy’s favourite; velutī is the fuller form.

Examples

  • assimulābō, quasi nunc exeam

    I’ll pretend I’m just coming outTer. Eun. 3.2.8 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quod est ventūrum, sapiēns quasi praesēns cavet.

    The wise man guards against what is coming as if it were here.Publ. Tur. Q 4

  • parvī enim prīmō ortū sīc jacent, tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint

    for at first, just born, little ones lie as if they had no mind at allCic. Fin. 5.42

  • ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

    I talk to you as I talk to myselfCic. Att. 8.14.2

  • velut sī prōlāpsus cecidisset, terram ōsculō contigit

    as if he had stumbled and fallen, he touched the earth with a kissLiv. 1.56.12
